commitResults.messageTitle: changing all instances of Duke to Floppy

commitResults.messageBody:
Malformed commands can terminate the chatbot or create incomplete tasks.

Keep the conversation running by validating task numbers and required
fields. Report errors through a domain-specific exception so command
failures have consistent, user-friendly messages.

The chatbot can add and update tasks but cannot remove obsolete items.

Add the delete command and replace the fixed-size array with a dynamic
task collection. This keeps task numbering contiguous after removals and
removes the artificial one-hundred-task limit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Represent task types with an enum
commitResults.messageBody:
Task categories are encoded separately in each subclass, which repeats
display logic and makes the supported set harder to inspect.

Represent the closed set of task categories with an enum and let the
base task format its type symbol. This keeps category metadata in one
place while preserving each subclass's specialised details.

Tasks exist only in memory, so closing the chatbot discards the user's
list.

Save every task-list change to a relative data path and restore it on
startup. Create missing directories automatically and reject malformed
stored records with a clear application error.

Task persistence is complete and verified on its dedicated increment
branch.

Merge the branch without fast-forwarding so the Level-7 development
history remains visible, as required by the project workflow.

Deadline and event dates are plain strings, so invalid values cannot be
detected or handled as calendar dates.

Parse ISO dates into LocalDate values, reject invalid ranges, and display
them in a readable format. Keep the stored form ISO-based so saved data
remains stable and unambiguous.

Date parsing and formatting are complete on the dedicated Level-8
branch.

Merge the branch without fast-forwarding so the increment remains
visible in the project history and can be detected by course tooling.

The main class handles input, parsing, task storage, list operations, and
output, which makes each change affect unrelated concerns.

Extract focused parser, UI, task-list, and command classes while keeping
storage separate. Let the main class coordinate these collaborators so
each responsibility can evolve and be tested independently.

The OOP refactoring is complete on its isolated branch.

Merge the branch without fast-forwarding to retain the design increment's
history while returning master to a complete working state.

The project needs a reproducible build before tests and distributable
artifacts can be added.

Merge the course-provided Gradle branch to preserve its supplied wrapper
and build configuration as a distinct history line.

The supplied Gradle setup targets the original Duke entry point and relies
on a locally installed Java 25 runtime.

Point application tasks at Floppy and provision Java 25 through Gradle's
official toolchain resolver. Name the generated artifact after the product
so builds and distributions are immediately identifiable.

Parsing and persistence contain the highest-risk input and data handling
logic, but regressions are detected only through manual testing.

Add focused JUnit tests for valid commands, malformed input, date ranges,
missing files, corrupted records, and multi-type save/load round trips.
These cases protect both classes' core behaviour.

The source follows the course convention, but future changes have no
automated guard against formatting and documentation regressions.

Integrate Checkstyle into the Gradle check lifecycle with rules derived
from the SE-EDU intermediate standard. Keep the permitted three-part
JUnit naming form while enforcing production naming and layout rules.

Users must scan the full task list when looking for related work.

Add a find command that searches descriptions case-insensitively and
shows matching tasks in their original order. Cover parsing, empty input,
partial matches, case differences, and no-result searches with tests.

Automated coding-standard enforcement is complete on its parallel branch.

Merge it first so subsequent increment merges are checked against the same
SE-EDU rules.

Keyword search is complete and tested on its parallel increment branch.

Merge it without fast-forwarding so the independent Level-9 work remains
visible while master receives the finished feature.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align Checkstyle with the course configuration
commitResults.messageBody: Replace the reduced rule subset with the course-referenced checks and test suppressions so production and test code receive consistent coding-standard enforcement.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaFX interface for task management
commitResults.messageBody: Present the existing chatbot through an FXML-based conversation window while preserving the console interface and shared command logic. Include cross-platform JavaFX dependencies, packaged resources, and response tests so the GUI remains portable and verifiable.
The GUI increment is complete on its dedicated branch but master does not yet contain it. Merge the verified work so all Week 5 parallel branches start from the latest completed application baseline.

Several private methods rely on values that their callers have already validated, but those assumptions are not visible in the code. This makes future maintenance more error-prone because an invalid internal call can fail far from its source.

Add Java assertions for command execution, parsed indexes, ordered event dates, and storage helper inputs. Keep normal validation and exceptions for user-provided data because assertions document programmer invariants and may be disabled at runtime.

The console and JavaFX entry points repeat command parsing, exit handling, execution, and error reporting. The duplicated control flow can drift and produce different behavior for the same command.

Extract one command-processing path shared by both interfaces. Keep presentation behind the Ui parameter so the refactoring removes duplication without coupling the application logic to JavaFX.

commitResults.messageTitle: Express task filtering as a stream pipeline
commitResults.messageBody:
Task search performs a direct collection transformation: retain tasks whose descriptions contain a normalized keyword and return the results. The manual accumulation loop obscures that intent with mutation.

Use a stream filter followed by toList() to state the transformation directly. The resulting list remains unmodifiable, preserving the method's existing encapsulation guarantee.
Add assertions for internal invariants
